description: Main window: core defaults; open/save dialogs and the plugin's message dialog (the question before unsaved changes are discarded: the plugin replaces window.confirm with an asynchronous one that needs it); reading and writing files, limited to the paths the user picked in a dialog or dropped on the window (lane 6). The app's own commands (device_public_key, device_sign, open_external) are allowed by default; the opener plugin is driven from Rust, so no opener, shell or http permission is granted to the webview (lane 8). Plugins (lane 11): reading and writing under $APPDATA (installed plugins live in $APPDATA/plugins) and listing folders the user picked in a dialog (Load unpacked folder). Closing over unsaved changes (lane 35): the page hears the shell's sawhorse://close-requested event (core:default's event listening), asks with the message dialog above, and answers through the app's own close_guard command, which also carries File > Exit; the shell closes or destroys the window itself, so no core:window permission (close, destroy) is granted to the webview.
